paragraphs.text: A student is on her way to a lesson, and everything goes wrong. Five pictures, five captions — read the pictures first and the captions will mostly confirm what you already guessed.

Three of the five captions hinge on one small word. {{de:kein Fahrrad}}, {{de:kein Bus}}, {{de:Keine Fahrkarte}} — when German denies that a thing is there, it does not reach for a separate "not". It changes the article, and the changed article already carries the meaning.

turns.speaker: Bild A
turns.german: Oje, kein Fahrrad! Schnell, da ist ein Bus!
turns.english: Oh no, no bicycle! Quick, there's a bus!

turns.speaker: Bild B
turns.german: Ach nee, kein Bus. Also schnell! Wo ist die U-Bahn?
turns.english: Oh no, no bus. Hurry then! Where's the subway?

turns.speaker: Bild D
turns.german: Ich gehe zu Fuß. Jetzt aber schnell!
turns.english: I'll walk. Then let's be quick about it!

turns.speaker: Bild E
turns.german: Heute kein Test! So ein Glück!
turns.english: No test today! What a stroke of luck!

paragraphs.text: The negation article fills exactly the slot where ein or eine would stand. Ask yourself first which indefinite article the noun would take if the thing were there — then take its negated twin: kein for masculine and neuter, keine for feminine and for the plural.
maskulin: kein Bus · neutrum: kein Fahrrad · feminin: keine U-Bahn · Plural: keine Autos

The noun itself stays untouched; only the article picks up the -e ending for feminine and plural. And there is a second use you already heard in the taxi: kein also corrects a wrong guess, as in "no, that is not a lake — that is a river".

examples.german: Ist das ein Bus? Nein, das ist kein Bus.
examples.english: Is that a bus? No, that is not a bus.

examples.german: Ist das eine Kirche? Nein, das ist keine Kirche, das ist das Rathaus.
examples.english: Is that a church? No, that is not a church, that is the town hall.

examples.german: Sind das Busse? Nein, das sind keine Busse.
examples.english: Are those buses? No, those are not buses.

blocks.prompt: The picture shows a bus, not a subway. Which answer is correct?
options: Nein, das ist nicht eine U-Bahn.
blocks.explanationEnglish: U-Bahn is feminine, so the negation carries the -e: keine U-Bahn. After kein the noun keeps its bare form — there is no second article in front of it.

concept.title: kein = nicht ein
concept.rule: kein replaces ein or eine when you deny that a thing is there. Feminine and plural nouns take keine; masculine and neuter take kein. The noun itself never changes.
concept.exampleGerman: Nein, das ist keine U-Bahn, das ist ein Bus.
concept.exampleEnglish: No, that is not a subway, that is a bus.
